name: N,N-Diethyl-6-methylergoline-8-carboxamide
summary: 9,10-Dihydro-LSD, or 9,10-DH-LSD, also known simply as dihydro-LSD (DH-LSD) or as 9,10-dihydrolysergic acid diethylamide, is a non-hallucinogenic serotonin receptor modulator of the lysergamide family related to lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD). It is the analogue of LSD in which the 9,10- double bond in the D ring of the ergoline ring system has been hydrogenated.

pharmacology.text: 9,10-Dihydro-LSD has been shown to bind to the serotonin 5-HT2A, 5-HT2C, and 5-HT1A receptors. It acts as a partial agonist of the serotonin 5-HT2A receptor similarly to LSD, whereas functional activities at the other serotonin receptors were not reported.
pharmacology.kind: Serotonin receptor modulator; Non-hallucinogenic serotonin 5-HT2A receptor partial agonist

uses.text: 9,10-Dihydro-LSD has been found to be inactive in terms of psychedelic effects in humans.

fact.en: It differs from LSD by just two hydrogen atoms added across one double bond, yet that small change is enough to remove LSD's psychedelic effects in people.
fact.zh: 它與 LSD 的差別只是在一個雙鍵上多加了兩個氫原子，但這個小小的改變就足以讓它在人體失去 LSD 的迷幻作用。
fact.zhHans: 它与 LSD 的差别只是在一个双键上多加了两个氢原子，但这个小小的改变就足以让它在人体失去 LSD 的迷幻作用。
